### "print -\t"
% print -
-a  -- with -c/-C, print arguments across before down
-b  -- recognise bindkey escape sequences
-c  -- print arguments in columns
-C  -- print arguments in specified number of columns
-D  -- substitute any arguments which are named directories using ~ notation
-f  -- print arguments as for the printf builtin
-i  -- case-insensitive sorting
-l  -- print arguments separated by newlines
-m  -- remove arguments not matching specified pattern
-n  -- do not add a newline to the result
-N  -- print arguments separated and terminated by nulls
-o  -- sort arguments in ascending order
-O  -- sort arguments in descending order
-P  -- perform prompt expansion
-R  -- emulate BSD echo (no escapes, -n & -e flags only)
-r  -- ignore escape conventions of echo
-s  -- place results in the history list
-S  -- place results in the history list, after splitting argument into word
-u  -- specify file descriptor to print arguments to
-v  -- store output in named parameter
-X  -- expand all tabs
-x  -- expand leading tabs
-z  -- push arguments onto editing buffer stack
@ 0,9
